The Router was also correct to mark stem/leaf checkpoints as untestable due to the macro crop. However, the Router was slightly lenient on the 'flat, circular pattern' checkpoint; the petals are not just non-flat, they are volumetrically stacked, which is a significant structural deviation from the 'daisy' prototype.

While the fine_grained_classifier predicted 'daisy' with high confidence, this reflects the model's loose classification rather than strict taxonomic adherence. The visible features (multi-layer petals, broad shape) align more closely with chrysanthemums or asters. Only 3 out of 5 testable checkpoints passed (center presence, general petal radiation), but the failure of the primary structural definition ('single whorl') heavily penalizes the score.

The primary issue is the 'melting' or fusion of the yellow center into the white petals, lacking the granular separation of real disc florets (Severity ~2.0).
